The '''2022–23 season''' was [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|119th season in existence]] and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|92nd consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. In addition to the [[2022–23 La Liga|domestic league]], Real Madrid participated in this season's editions of the [[2022–23 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2023 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], and the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. As the reigning [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|European champions]], they contested the [[2022 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]], winning 2–0 and claiming a [[List of UEFA Super Cup finals#Performances|record-equalling]] fifth title, and then went on to win a [[FIFA Club World Cup#Performances by club|record-extending]] fifth [[2022 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] title in February 2023.

Real Madrid did not play any official matches between 10 November and 30 December due to a mid-season break in accommodation of the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in Qatar. La Liga was suspended after matchday 14,<ref>{{cite news|last=Astbury|first=Matt|title=What does the winter World Cup in Qatar mean for the 2022/23 La Liga season?|url=https://www.dazn.com/en-US/news/soccer/what-does-the-winter-world-cup-in-qatar-mean-for-the-202223-la-liga-season/sqinccp68nyu17etkq9lrnlee|publisher=DAZN|date=1 August 2022|access-date=30 August 2022|archive-date=22 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922101454/https://www.dazn.com/en-US/news/soccer/what-does-the-winter-world-cup-in-qatar-mean-for-the-202223-la-liga-season/sqinccp68nyu17etkq9lrnlee|url-status=live}}</ref> and the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League group stage|Champions League group stage]] wrapped up earlier than usual, at the beginning of November.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hall|first=Andy|title=How will the 2022 World Cup affect the Champions League schedule?|url=https://en.as.com/soccer/how-will-the-2022-world-cup-affect-the-champions-league-schedule-n/|publisher=AS|date=25 August 2022|access-date=30 August 2022|archive-date=25 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825224325/https://en.as.com/soccer/how-will-the-2022-world-cup-affect-the-champions-league-schedule-n/|url-status=live}}</ref>

This season was the first since [[2005–06 Real Madrid CF season|2005–06]] without [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]], who departed as a free agent in the summer, first since [[2012–13 Real Madrid CF season|2012–13]] without [[Gareth Bale]] and [[Isco]], and the first season since [[2014–15 Real Madrid CF season|2014–15]] without [[Casemiro]], who departed to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].

==Summary==
===Pre-season===
On 1 June, right after the conclusion of the 2021–22 season, the club announced the departures of [[Isco]] and [[Gareth Bale]] due to the expiration of their contracts, both players having spent nine seasons playing for ''Los Blancos''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Whitehead|first=Jacob|title=Isco announces Real Madrid exit|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4176543/2022/05/30/isco-announces-real-madrid-exit-this-summer-after-contract-expiration/|publisher=The Athletic|date=30 May 2022|access-date=30 May 2022|archive-date=20 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220620141604/https://theathletic.com/news/isco-announces-real-madrid-exit/OQAiQ3y1y7Yb/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Bosher|first=Luke|title=Gareth Bale confirms Real Madrid exit: 'I realised a dream, it has been an incredible experience'|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3490537/2022/06/01/gareth-bale-confirms-real-madrid-exit-i-realised-a-dream-it-has-been-an-incredible-experience/|publisher=The Athletic|access-date=1 June 2022|date=1 June 2022|archive-date=4 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104190815/https://theathletic.com/3490537/2022/06/01/gareth-bale-confirms-real-madrid-exit-i-realised-a-dream-it-has-been-an-incredible-experience/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 2 June, Madrid announced the arrival of [[Antonio Rüdiger]] on a free transfer from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], with the German signing a four-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Antonio Rudiger: Real Madrid to sign Chelsea defender on free transfer after agreeing four-year deal|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12626023/antonio-rudiger-real-madrid-to-sign-chelsea-defender-on-free-transfer-after-agreeing-four-year-deal|publisher=Sky Sports|date=2 June 2022|access-date=2 June 2022|archive-date=30 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220630032308/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12626023/antonio-rudiger-real-madrid-to-sign-chelsea-defender-on-free-transfer-after-agreeing-four-year-deal|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 June, [[Luka Modrić]] renewed his contract with Real Madrid until 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Official Announcement: Modrić|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/06/08/official-announcement-modri%C4%87|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=8 June 2022|access-date=8 June 2022|archive-date=28 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220628084841/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/06/08/official-announcement-modri%C4%87|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid announced the signing of [[Aurélien Tchouaméni]] from [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]], penning a six-year contract with the player.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Kallas|first1=Fernando|last2=Pathak|first2=Manasi|title=Real Madrid reach agreement to sign Tchouameni from Monaco on six-year deal|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/real-madrid-reach-agreement-sign-tchouameni-monaco-six-year-deal-2022-06-11/|publisher=Reuters|date=11 June 2022|access-date=11 June 2022|archive-date=11 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220611174422/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/real-madrid-reach-agreement-sign-tchouameni-monaco-six-year-deal-2022-06-11/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 12 June, Madrid announced the departure of the team's captain, [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]], after 15 years of service; he won 25 titles with Real Madrid, more than any other player in the history of the club.<ref>{{Cite web|last=König|first=Kosta|title=Real Madrid announce Marcelo exit and farewell date|url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/realmadrid-2022-06-12-real-madrid-announce-marcelo-exit-and-farewell-date/|publisher=Tribuna|date=12 June 2022|access-date=12 June 2022|archive-date=4 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104190817/https://tribuna.com/en/news/realmadrid-2022-06-12-real-madrid-announce-marcelo-exit-and-farewell-date/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Marcelo enhances his legendary status: 25 trophies with Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/05/29/marcelo-enhances-his-legendary-status-25-trophies-with-real-madrid|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=29 May 2022|access-date=12 June 2022|archive-date=2 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220802013159/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/05/29/marcelo-enhances-his-legendary-status-25-trophies-with-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 July, the club announced that they had reached an agreement with [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] for the permanent transfer of [[Luka Jović]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Announcement: Jović|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/07/08/official-announcement-jovi%C4%87|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=8 July 2022|access-date=8 July 2022|archive-date=8 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708215057/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/07/08/official-announcement-jovi%C4%87|url-status=live}}</ref> Eleven days later, Madrid announced the departure of [[Takefusa Kubo]] to [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Announcement: Kubo|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/07/19/official-announcement-kubo|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=19 July 2022|access-date=19 July 2022|archive-date=19 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220719161606/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/07/19/official-announcement-kubo|url-status=live}}</ref> On 1 August, [[Borja Mayoral]] left the club to join [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on a permanent transfer.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Announcement: Borja Mayoral|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/08/01/official-announcement-borja-mayoral|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=1 August 2022|access-date=1 August 2022|archive-date=10 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220810165512/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/08/01/official-announcement-borja-mayoral|url-status=live}}</ref>

===August===
On 10 August, Real Madrid opened the season with a 2–0 victory over [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] in the [[2022 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]]. [[David Alaba]] and [[Karim Benzema]] scored the goals, with the latter breaking the tie with [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] and becoming the club's outright [[List of Real Madrid CF records and statistics#Goalscorers|second-highest]] goalscorer. The win marked Madrid's fifth [[UEFA Super Cup|European Super Cup]] title, a [[List of UEFA Super Cup finals#Performances|tournament record]] shared with [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Bysouth|first=Alex|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Eintracht Frankfurt: Karim Benzema scores 324th goal for Real in Super Cup win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62475679|publisher=BBC|date=10 August 2022|access-date=10 August 2022|archive-date=10 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230610060356/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62475679|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, [[Lucas Vázquez]] and Alaba scored two second-half goals, as Madrid started their [[2022–23 La Liga|La Liga]] title defense with a 2–1 win at [[UD Almería|Almería]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Almería 1–2 Real Madrid: Substitute David Alaba scores with first touch to give champions comeback win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62544352|publisher=BBC|date=14 August 2022|access-date=14 August 2022|archive-date=14 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814223714/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62544352|url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 August, the club announced an agreement with [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on the transfer of [[Casemiro]], who spent nine years at Real Madrid and won 18 trophies.<ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Casemiro|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/08/19/official-announcement-casemiro|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=19 August 2022|access-date=19 August 2022|archive-date=20 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220820203029/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/08/19/official-announcement-casemiro|url-status=live}}</ref> On 20 August, [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] was beaten 4–1 on the road, with Benzema, [[Luka Modrić]], [[Vinícius Júnior]] and [[Federico Valverde]] on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|title=Celta Vigo 1–4 Real Madrid: Luka Modrić and Vinícius Jr score in La Liga win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62620974|publisher=BBC|date=20 August 2022|access-date=20 August 2022|archive-date=21 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220821134454/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62620974|url-status=live}}</ref> Eight days later, a goal from Vinícius and a late Benzema brace got Madrid a 3–1 win at [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], their third straight away win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Espanyol 1–3 Real Madrid: Karim Benzema scores twice as Real win thriller|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62709201|publisher=BBC|date=28 August 2022|access-date=28 August 2022|archive-date=29 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220829044416/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62709201|url-status=live}}</ref>

===September===
On the third day of the new month, goals from Vinícius and [[Rodrygo]] secured Madrid a 2–1 win over [[Real Betis]] at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]], ending a five-year winless and goalless home run against ''Los Verdiblancos''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Real Betis: Hosts continue perfect La Liga start|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62782711|publisher=BBC|date=3 September 2022|access-date=3 September 2022|archive-date=5 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005073019/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62782711|url-status=live}}</ref> On 6 September, Madrid faced [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] away from home in the first match of the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] and won 3–0, with Vinícius, Modrić and [[Eden Hazard]] scoring the goals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Duncan|first=Thomas|title=Celtic 0–3 Real Madrid: Champions League holders show class in clinical showing|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62771360|publisher=BBC|date=6 September 2022|access-date=6 September 2022|archive-date=15 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230815162537/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62771360|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, a strike from Valverde and goals from Vinícius, Rodrygo and Rüdiger, a debut one for the German, earned Real a 4–1 home victory over [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Mallorca: Federico Valverde, Vinícius Jr, Rodrygo and Antonio Rüdiger score|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62869010|publisher=BBC|date=11 September 2022|access-date=11 September 2022|archive-date=11 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220911143054/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62869010|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 September, Madrid defeated [[RB Leipzig]] 2–0 at home on matchday 2 of the Champions League, thanks to goals from Valverde and [[Marco Asensio]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–0 RB Leipzig: Federico Valverde and Marco Asensio score late goals|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62894698|publisher=BBC|date=14 September 2022|access-date=14 September 2022|archive-date=13 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220913165817/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62894698|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Rodrygo and Valverde scored two first-half goals for a 2–1 away win against [[Atlético Madrid]] in the [[Madrid derby]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlético Madrid 1–2 Real Madrid: La Liga champions keep up 100% start to season|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62950553|publisher=BBC|date=18 September 2022|access-date=18 September 2022|archive-date=18 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220918212653/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62950553|url-status=live}}</ref>

===October===
After the [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]], play resumed on 2 October and Madrid's winning run came to an end after a 1–1 home draw against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], with Vinícius scoring the only goal for the team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kirkland|first=Alex|title=Benzema returns from injury but his off night, missed penalty show Real Madrid aren't infallible|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/real-madrid-espreal_madrid/story/4760031/benzema-back-but-real-madrids-perfect-season-ends-in-draw|publisher=ESPN|date=2 October 2022|access-date=2 October 2022|archive-date=2 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002221118/https://www.espn.com/soccer/real-madrid-espreal_madrid/story/4760031/benzema-back-but-real-madrids-perfect-season-ends-in-draw|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, goals from Rodrygo and Vinícius gave Madrid a 2–1 home win over [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] in the third matchday of the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web|last=Magee|first=Will|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Shakhtar Donetsk: Rodrygo Goes and Vinícius Jr both score as Real Madrid maintain 100% record with Shakhtar Donetsk win|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/champions-league/2021-2022/real-madrid-v-shakhtar-donetsk-champions-league-live_sto9170532/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=5 October 2022|access-date=5 October 2022|archive-date=4 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204044714/https://www.eurosport.com/football/champions-league/2021-2022/real-madrid-v-shakhtar-donetsk-champions-league-live_sto9170532/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 October, Madrid registered a 1–0 win at Getafe, with the lone goal being scored by [[Éder Militão]] in the third minute.<ref>{{cite web|title=Getafe 0–1 Real Madrid: Éder Militão header sends Los Blancos top of La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63186835|publisher=BBC|date=8 October 2022|access-date=8 October 2022|archive-date=8 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008211637/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63186835|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Real played Shakhtar Donetsk in a Champions League game in Poland and came away with a 1–1 draw, thanks to an [[Association football#Duration and tie-breaking methods|injury time]] goal from Rüdiger, which also officially qualified them for the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|round of 16]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Shakhtar Donetsk 1–1 Real Madrid: Antonio Rüdiger goal takes reigning champions into last 16|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63209183|publisher=BBC|date=11 October 2022|access-date=11 October 2022|archive-date=10 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221010214058/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63209183|url-status=live}}</ref> On 16 October, Madrid won the first [[El Clásico]] of the season, beating [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] 3–1 at the Santiago Bernabéu with goals from Benzema, Valverde and Rodrygo.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=El Clasico: Real Madrid beat Barcelona 3–1 at Bernabeu|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63270650|publisher=BBC|date=16 October 2022|access-date=16 October 2022|archive-date=16 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016005846/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63270650|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid defeated [[Elche CF|Elche]] 3–0 away from home, with Valverde, Benzema and Asensio on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|title=Elche 0–3 Real Madrid: Karim Benzema celebrates Ballon d'Or award with goal in win for Carlo Ancelotti's side|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/elche-v-real-madrid-la-liga-live_sto9191645/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=19 October 2022|access-date=19 October 2022|archive-date=15 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415123652/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> On 22 October, [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] was beaten at the Bernabéu, as goals from Modrić, Vázquez and Valverde gave Madrid a suffered 3–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web|last=Van Ristell|first=Ethan|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Sevilla: Luka Modrić, Lucas Vázquez and Federico Valverde on target as Real remain unbeaten|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/la-liga-live_sto9195723/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=22 October 2022|access-date=22 October 2022|archive-date=15 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415123738/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid got defeated 2–3 in an away Champions League game against RB Leipzig, with the two goals being scored by Vinícius and Rodrygo. This loss was their first in the season, also ending the team's twenty-game unbeaten streak.<ref>{{cite web|title=RB Leipzig 3–2 Real Madrid: European champions suffer first defeat of the season|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63394769|publisher=BBC|date=25 October 2022|access-date=25 October 2022|archive-date=25 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221025211551/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63394769|url-status=live}}</ref> On 30 October, Madrid dropped points against [[Girona FC|Girona]] at home. The game ended tied at 1–1, with Vinícius initially giving Real the lead before [[Cristhian Stuani]] equalised it with a penalty for the guests.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 1–1 Girona: Toni Kroos sent off as champions go top with draw|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63447920|publisher=BBC|date=30 October 2022|access-date=30 October 2022|archive-date=30 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221030174735/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63447920|url-status=live}}</ref>

===November===
On the second day of the new month, Real Madrid produced a 5–1 home victory over Celtic in the Champions League and advanced to the round of 16 as group winners. Modrić, Rodrygo, Asensio, Vinícius and Valverde each scored one goal.<ref>{{cite web|last=Burke|first=Andy|title=Real Madrid 5–1 Celtic: Scottish champions routed in final group game Madrid|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63447097|publisher=BBC|date=2 November 2022|access-date=2 November 2022|archive-date=1 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221101213515/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63447097|url-status=live}}</ref> On 7 November, the league match at [[Rayo Vallecano]] ended in a 2–3 loss, as Madrid gave away the league's number one spot to their rivals Barcelona. Modrić and Militão scored to give Madrid a temporary 2–1 lead. This was Real's first La Liga loss of the season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Azzoni|first=Tales|title=Rayo Vallecano hands Real Madrid first Spanish league loss|url=https://apnews.com/article/soccer-sports-la-liga-madrid-real-6ee7d387d19c6ab547af017d7435644b|publisher=Associated Press|date=7 November 2022|access-date=7 November 2022|archive-date=7 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221107231151/https://apnews.com/article/soccer-sports-la-liga-madrid-real-6ee7d387d19c6ab547af017d7435644b|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid managed to beat [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] in their last game before the World Cup break, winning 2–1 at home after Militão's header and a strike from [[Toni Kroos]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Cádiz: Éder Militão and Toni Kroos score as Carlo Ancelotti's team close gap on Barcelona|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/real-madrid-v-cadiz-fc-la-liga-live_sto9217847/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=10 November 2022|access-date=10 November 2022|archive-date=10 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221110225204/https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/real-madrid-v-cadiz-fc-la-liga-live_sto9217847/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

===December===
Ancelotti's side returned to action on 30 December after a 1.5 month break for the World Cup and managed to beat [[Real Valladolid]] away 2–0 in what was the only match of the month, with Benzema scoring a late brace to end the year on a high.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rooke|first=Sam|title=Real Valladolid 0–2 Real Madrid: Karim Benzema fires champions to victory on the road|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/real-valladolid-v-real-madrid-la-liga-live_sto9289083/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=30 December 2022|access-date=30 December 2022|archive-date=15 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415123654/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

===January===
The new year kicked off with the start of the [[2022–23 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] on 3 January, which Madrid joined in the round of 32. The team travelled to [[Segunda Federación|fourth-tier]] [[CP Cacereño|Cacereño]], winning there 1–0, thanks to a solo Rodrygo goal, and progressing to the round of 16.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hilsum|first=James|title=Copa del Rey: Rodrygo stunner sees Real Madrid edge out fourth-tier Cacereño and progress to last 16|url=https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/copa-del-rey/2022-2023/copa-del-rey-rodrygo-stunner-real-madrid-edge-out-fourth-tier-cacereno-and-progress-to-last-16_sto9298738/story.shtml|publisher=Eusrosport|date=3 January 2023|access-date=3 January 2023|archive-date=15 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415123616/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid lost 1–2 in the away league match against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], with the only goal coming from Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid miss chance to top LaLiga in narrow loss to Villarreal|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/spanish-primera-division/story/4845379/real-madrid-miss-chance-to-top-laliga-in-narrow-loss-to-villarreal|publisher=ESPN|date=7 January 2023|access-date=7 January 2023|archive-date=5 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405215435/https://www.espn.com/soccer/spanish-primera-division/story/4845379/real-madrid-miss-chance-to-top-laliga-in-narrow-loss-to-villarreal|url-status=live}}</ref> This match also marked the first time in its history that the club fielded a line-up with no Spanish players.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rai |first1=Guillermo |title=No Spaniards in the XI a first for Real Madrid, but the big concerns lie elsewhere |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4068673/2023/01/09/real-madrid-on-field-problems/ |website=The New York Times |access-date=20 July 2026 |date=10 January 2023}}</ref> On 11 January, Madrid defeated [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] 4–3 in a penalty shootout of the first [[2023 Supercopa de España]] semi-final to advance to the [[2023 Supercopa de España final|final]], after the extra time ended 1–1, as Benzema scored the only goal for Ancelotti's team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 1–1 Valencia: Los Blancos advance to Supercopa final with penalty shoot-out win over Gennaro Gattuso's side|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/spanish-supercopa/2022-2023/supercopa-de-espana-live-real-madrid-v-valencia_sto9308663/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=11 January 2023|access-date=11 January 2023|archive-date=15 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415123656/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> On 15 January, Madrid suffered a 1–3 defeat in the Supercopa de España final against Barcelona, with the only goal coming from a Benzema strike in injury time. This was Real's first Clásico loss in a Spanish Super Cup match since [[2012–13 Real Madrid CF season|August 2012]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 1–3 Barcelona: Gavi stars as Xavi secures first trophy with Spanish Super Cup win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64268835|publisher=BBC|date=15 January 2023|access-date=15 January 2023|archive-date=1 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230201010425/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64268835|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid progressed to the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey, thanks to a 3–2 comeback win over Villarreal, trailing 0–2 at half-time. The goals came from Vinícius, Militão and [[Dani Ceballos]], as Real ended a six-match winless run at the [[Estadio de la Cerámica]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Walker-Roberts|first=James|title=Villarreal 2–3 Real Madrid: Dani Ceballos inspires Copa del Rey comeback with goal and assist for Vinicius Junior|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/copa-del-rey/2022-2023/villarreal-2-3-real-madrid-dani-ceballos-inspires-copa-del-rey-comeback-with-goal-and-assist-for-vin_sto9335691/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=19 January 2023|access-date=19 January 2023|archive-date=15 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415123616/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> On 22 January, Benzema and Kroos scored two goals to give Madrid a 2–0 [[El Viejo Clásico]] win at [[Athletic Bilbao]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Athletic Bilbao 0–2 Real Madrid: Karim Benzema volley helps seal victory|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64367946|publisher=BBC|date=22 January 2023|access-date=22 January 2023|archive-date=22 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230122221413/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64367946|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid produced a comeback versus Atlético Madrid at home, winning 3–1 to book their place in the Copa del Rey semi-finals, thanks to a score-equaling Rodrygo shot and overtime goals from Benzema and Vinícius.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Atlético Madrid: Karim Benzema and Vinicius net extra-time goals to set up Copa del Rey win|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/copa-del-rey/2022-2023/copa-del-rey-live-real-madrid-v-atletico-madrid_sto9347127/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=26 January 2023|access-date=26 January 2023}}</ref> On 29 January, Madrid's home game against [[Real Sociedad]] ended in a goalless stalemate, as Real failed to score for the first time in the season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Barton|first=Aaron|title=Real Madrid 0–0 Real Sociedad: Stalemate at the Bernabeu as La Real frustrate Madrid in La Liga title chase setback|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/real-madrid-v-real-sociedad-la-liga-live_sto9356647/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=29 January 2023|access-date=29 January 2023|archive-date=7 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230307170638/https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/real-madrid-v-real-sociedad-la-liga-live_sto9356647/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

===February===
The month began for Madrid on 2 February, after Asensio and Vinícius scored twice in the second half for a 2–0 win over Valencia at the Bernabéu.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Valencia: Madrid cut Barcelona's lead at top of La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64500528|publisher=BBC|date=2 February 2023|access-date=2 February 2023|archive-date=2 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202200224/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64500528|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid suffered their third league defeat of the season, losing 0–1 away to Mallorca.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mallorca 1–0 Real Madrid: Asensio misses penalty in La Liga shock|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64531070|publisher=BBC|date=5 February 2023|access-date=5 February 2023|archive-date=5 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230205161732/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64531070|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 February, goals from Vinícius, Valverde, Rodrygo and [[Sergio Arribas (footballer, born 2001)|Sergio Arribas]], a debut one for the [[Real Madrid Castilla|club's academy]] player, helped Madrid to take a smashing 4–1 victory over [[Al Ahly SC|Al Ahly]] in the semi-finals of the [[2022 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Chiu|first=Nigel|title=Al Ahly 1–4 Real Madrid: La Liga giants given mid-match scare as they reach Club World Cup final|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/club-world-cup/2022/al-ahly-1-4-real-madrid-la-liga-giants-given-mid-match-scare-as-they-reach-club-world-cup-final_sto9379512/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=8 February 2023|access-date=8 February 2023}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid claimed a [[FIFA Club World Cup#Performances by club|record-extending]] fifth Club World Cup title, beating [[Al-Hilal Saudi FC|Al-Hilal]] 5–3 in the [[2022 FIFA Club World Cup final|final]], with braces from Vinícius and Valverde and a Benzema goal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 5–3 Al-Hilal: Vinicius & Federico Valverde score in Club World Cup final win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64612995|publisher=BBC|date=11 February 2023|access-date=11 February 2023|archive-date=15 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215230119/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64612995|url-status=live}}</ref> On 15 February, Madrid got a 4–0 home win over Elche, with Asensio, Benzema twice from the penalty spot and Modrić all on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Barton|first=Aaron|title=Real Madrid 4–0 Elche: Karim Benzema double puts hosts back on track in La Liga|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/real-madrid-4-0-elche-karim-benzema-double-puts-hosts-back-on-track-in-la-liga_sto9391559/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=15 February 2023|access-date=15 February 2023}}</ref> Three days later, two late goals from Valverde and Asensio earned Madrid a 2–0 league win at Osasuna.<ref>{{cite web|last=Southby|first=Ben|title=Osasuna 0–2 Real Madrid: Federico Valverde and Marco Asensio on target as Carlo Ancelotti's side overcome hosts|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/osasuna-v-real-madrid-la-liga-live_sto9399715/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=18 February 2023|access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref> On 21 February, Madrid met [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at the [[Anfield]] in the first leg of the Champions League round of 16. Trailing 0–2 in the very beginning of the match, Real managed to take a crushing 5–2 comeback victory, after two first-half goals from Vinícius were followed up by a Militão header and a brace from Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Liverpool 2–5 Real Madrid: Hosts thrashed by holders in Champions League last 16|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64708314|publisher=BBC|date=21 February 2023|access-date=21 February 2023|archive-date=20 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230220183237/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64708314|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, the third Madrid derby of the season against Atlético Madrid ended in a 1–1 draw at the Bernabéu, thanks to an equalizer by academy player [[Álvaro Rodríguez (footballer, born 2004)|Álvaro Rodríguez]], who scored his debut goal for the first team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 1–1 Atlético Madrid: Hosts' title hopes dealt further blow by rivals|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64772311|publisher=BBC|date=25 February 2023|access-date=25 February 2023|archive-date=25 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230225205356/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64772311|url-status=live}}</ref>

===March===
On the second day of the new month, the third Clásico of the season was lost 0–1 to Barcelona at home in the first leg of the Copa del Rey semi-finals, with an own goal from Militão being the only goal of the match.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Emma|title=Real Madrid 0–1 Barcelona: Éder Militão own goal gives Barca first-leg edge|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64829271|publisher=BBC|date=2 March 2023|access-date=2 March 2023|archive-date=2 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230302223435/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64829271|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid dropped points in a 0–0 away draw against Real Betis.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Betis 0–0 Real Madrid: Carlo Ancelotti's side nine points off top with draw|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64858015|publisher=BBC|date=5 March 2023|access-date=5 March 2023|archive-date=6 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306000944/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64858015|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 March, Madrid ended their three-match winless streak, beating Espanyol 3–1 at home, thanks to goals from Vinícius, Militão and Asensio.<ref>{{cite web|last=Iveson|first=Ali|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Espanyol: Vinícius Júnior, Éder Militão and Marco Asensio on target as Real pick up first win in four|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2022-2023/real-madrid-v-espanyol-la-liga-live_sto9502556/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=11 March 2023|access-date=11 March 2023|archive-date=15 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415124343/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, the home leg of the Champions League round of 16 was won 1–0 (6–2 on aggregate), with a Benzema goal sending Madrid through to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Real Madrid 1–0 Liverpool (6–2 agg): Reds dumped out of Champions League|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64959699|publisher=BBC|date=15 March 2023|access-date=15 March 2023|archive-date=14 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314214424/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64959699|url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 March, the crucial league Clásico was lost 1–2 away from home, with Real having opened the scoring via an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|last=Emons|first=Michael|title=Barcelona 2–1 Real Madrid: Franck Kessié scores late winner as Barca move 12 points clear|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64959699|publisher=BBC|date=19 March 2023|access-date=19 March 2023|archive-date=15 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230315222407/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64959699|url-status=live}}</ref>

===April===
Madrid kicked off the month with a 6–0 home win over Real Valladolid, as goal from Rodrygo and Benzema first-half hat-trick were followed by strikes from Asensio and Vázquez.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Real Madrid 6–0 Real Valladolid: Karim Benzema scores first-half hat-trick in big win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65156348|publisher=BBC|date=2 April 2023|access-date=2 April 2023|archive-date=2 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230402164313/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65156348|url-status=live}}</ref> On 5 April, Real achieved a 4–0 away victory over Barcelona in the return leg of the Copa del Rey semi-finals and advanced to the [[2023 Copa del Rey Final|final]] for the first time since [[2014 Copa del Rey Final|2014]]. Vinícius opened the scoring and Benzema then got his second hat-trick in a row.<ref>{{cite web|last=Drury|first=Sam|title=Barcelona 0–4 Real Madrid (1–4 agg): Karim Benzema hat-trick sends visitors to Copa del Rey final|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65196145|publisher=BBC|date=5 April 2023|access-date=5 April 2023|archive-date=5 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405212140/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65196145|url-status=live}}</ref> The final scoreline marked the first time that Madrid had scored at least four goals against Barcelona in any competition since a [[2007–08 Real Madrid CF season#Matches|4–1 La Liga victory]] in May 2008, and for the first time at the [[Camp Nou]] since a [[1962–63 Real Madrid CF season#Matches|5–1 league win]] in January 1963.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dominski|first=Michael|title=How Real Madrid beat Barcelona 4–0 in Clasico thanks to Benzema hat-trick to advance to Copa del Rey final|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/barcelona-real-madrid-live-score-updates-result-el-clasico/a0Bo6ALGLgLk/|publisher=The Athletic|date=5 April 2023|access-date=5 April 2023|url-access=subscription|archive-date=5 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405194122/https://theathletic.com/live-blogs/barcelona-real-madrid-live-score-updates-result-el-clasico/a0Bo6ALGLgLk/|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid suffered a 2–3 home loss to Villarreal, despite having been 2–1 up after an own goal and a Vinícius strike.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–3 Villarreal: Hosts' title hopes dealt huge blow with loss|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65223514|publisher=BBC|date=8 April 2023|access-date=8 April 2023|archive-date=8 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408211701/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65223514|url-status=live}}</ref> On 12 April, Madrid hosted [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at home in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-finals and beat the English side 2–0, as Benzema and Asensio got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Chelsea: Blues' Champions League ambitions dented by the holders|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65243061|publisher=BBC|date=12 April 2023|access-date=19 April 2023|archive-date=19 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230419164001/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65243061|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, goals from [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]] and Asensio gave Madrid a 2–0 away league win over Cádiz.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cádiz 0–2 Real Madrid: Carlo Ancelotti's side prepare for Chelsea tie with win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65289609|publisher=BBC|date=15 April 2023|access-date=19 April 2023|archive-date=18 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230418234409/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65289609|url-status=live}}</ref> On 18 April, Madrid played the Champions League quarter-finals return leg against Chelsea, getting another 2–0 win and progressing to the semi-finals 4–0 on aggregate, thanks to a Rodrygo brace.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chelsea 0–2 Real Madrid (0–4 agg): Blues exit Champions League as Real finish job|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65303856|publisher=BBC|date=18 April 2023|access-date=19 April 2023|archive-date=18 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230418234409/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65303856|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Ancelotti's side managed to beat Celta Vigo 2–0 at the Bernabéu with goals from Asensio and Militão.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Celta Vigo: Marco Asensio stars as Real win at home against Celta|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65360994|publisher=BBC|date=22 April 2023|access-date=24 April 2023|archive-date=23 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423225224/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65360994|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 April, Madrid suffered a 2–4 away defeat against Girona, with the goals being scored by Vinícius and Vazquez.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Girona 4–2 Real Madrid: Valentin Castellanos scores four in La Liga surprise|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65393573|publisher=BBC|date=25 April 2023|access-date=6 May 2023|archive-date=2 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230502220344/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65393573|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Benzema scored another first-half hat-trick, which was followed by a goal from Rodrygo, as Madrid sealed a 4–2 home win over Almería.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 4–2 Almería: Karim Benzema hits hat-trick as second-placed Real seal home win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65438399|publisher=BBC|date=29 April 2023|access-date=6 May 2023|archive-date=6 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230506012941/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65438399|url-status=live}}</ref>

===May===
The month began on a sour note on 2 May, when Real was beaten 0–2 by Real Sociedad at the [[Anoeta Stadium|Anoeta]] and dropped down to third place in the La Liga standings.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Sociedad 2–0 Real Madrid: Defeat leaves Barcelona on verge of La Liga title|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65465225|publisher=BBC|date=2 May 2023|access-date=6 May 2023|archive-date=6 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230506012943/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65465225|url-status=live}}</ref> But, fortunes improved four days later, when a brace from Rodrygo helped Madrid to triumph 2–1 over Osasuna in the Copa del Rey final at the [[Estadio La Cartuja]] in [[Seville]] for their first La Copa in 9 years, and Ancelotti's second with the club.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Osasuna: Rodrygo scores twice as Madrid win Copa del Rey|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65500297|publisher=BBC|date=6 May 2023|access-date=6 May 2023|archive-date=6 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230506031329/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65500297|url-status=live}}</ref> On 9 May, Madrid hosted [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the Champions League semi-finals first leg, rematching the last season's encounter at the same stage of the competition. The match ended in a 1–1 draw, as Vinícius scored a wondergoal from outside the box.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Real Madrid 1–1 Manchester City: Kevin de Bruyne helps City draw Champions League first leg|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65527338|publisher=BBC|date=9 May 2023|access-date=10 May 2023|archive-date=9 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509233506/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65527338|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, an Asensio goal secured three points against Getafe.<ref>{{cite web|title=Asensio gives depleted Real narrow win over Getafe|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/asensio-gives-depleted-real-narrow-win-over-getafe-2023-05-13/|publisher=Reuters|date=13 May 2023|access-date=13 May 2023|archive-date=14 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514015209/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/asensio-gives-depleted-real-narrow-win-over-getafe-2023-05-13/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 17 May, the return leg of the Champions League semi-final against Manchester City was played and Real were beaten by a scoreline of 0–4, knocking them out of the competition.<ref>{{cite web|title=Manchester City 4–0 Real Madrid: Pep Guardiola masterminds comprehensive win for rampant Citizens at Etihad|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/champions-league/2021-2022/manchester-city-v-real-madrid-champions-league-live_sto9607457/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|date=17 May 2023|access-date=17 May 2023|archive-date=9 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609163447/https://www.eurosport.com/football/champions-league/2021-2022/manchester-city-v-real-madrid-champions-league-live_sto9607457/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid lost an away game versus Valencia 0–1.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vinícius Jr suffers racist abuse and is sent off in Real Madrid 1–0 defeat at Valencia|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65666613|publisher=BBC|date=21 May 2023|access-date=25 May 2023|archive-date=14 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230614142333/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65666613|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 May, Ancelotti's team managed to beat Rayo Vallecano 2–1 at home, as Benzema and Rodrygo got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Rayo Vallecano: Madrid players and fans show support for Vinícius Jr in win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65703448|publisher=BBC|date=24 May 2023|access-date=25 May 2023|archive-date=25 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230525002045/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65703448|url-status=live}}</ref> A Rodrygo brace secured Madrid three points in a 2–1 win at Sevilla on 27 May.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rodrygo brace earns Madrid victory over Sevilla|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230527-rodrygo-brace-earns-madrid-victory-over-sevilla|publisher=france24.com|date=27 May 2023|access-date=27 May 2023|archive-date=27 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230527194524/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230527-rodrygo-brace-earns-madrid-victory-over-sevilla|url-status=live}}</ref>

===June===
In the last game of the season, on 4 June, Benzema scored his last goal for the club as the match against Athletic Bilbao ended in a 1–1 draw, which settled Madrid at the second place in the league.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 1–1 Athletic Bilbao: Karim Benzema scores on final appearance for club|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65805719|publisher=BBC|date=4 June 2023|access-date=4 June 2023|archive-date=4 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604184610/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65805719|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 10 June 2022, Real Madrid announced they would travel to the United States to participate in the pre-season Soccer Champions Tour.<ref>{{cite news|title=Schedule of Real Madrid's games in Soccer Champions Tour|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/schedule-of-real-madrids-games-in-soccer-champions-tour|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=10 June 2022|access-date=10 June 2022|archive-date=17 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317112121/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/schedule-of-real-madrids-games-in-soccer-champions-tour|url-status=live}}</ref> ''El Clásico'' against Barcelona marked the second time the teams face each other on American soil after the [[2017–18 Real Madrid CF season#Pre-season and friendlies|2017]] [[2017 International Champions Cup|International Champions Cup]] match.<ref>{{cite web|title=All about the Real Madrid v Barça clásico on the 2022 U.S.A. tour|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2647591/all-about-the-real-madrid-v-barca-clasico-on-the-2022-usa-tour/featured|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=16 June 2022|access-date=12 July 2022|archive-date=12 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220712120433/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2647591/all-about-the-real-madrid-v-barca-clasico-on-the-2022-usa-tour/featured|url-status=live}}</ref>
